::: {.block title="2. Is there hope for coastal regions?"}
![Left: R² by depth for profiles in open-ocean, slope and shelf water (ETOPO 2022 depth); bins with fewer than 3 floats or sites not drawn. Right: integrated CHLA, observed vs predicted. Held-out data, space-time split, Argo + OOI model.](figures/fig_coastal_skill.png){#fig-coastal script="scripts/fig_coastal_skill.py" width="100%"}

Skill falls with depth everywhere, and faster in shallow water: R² reaches
about 0 by 20 m on the shelf and by 50 m on the slope, but stays near 0.35
below 80 m in the open ocean. Integrated CHLA holds up better (R² 0.43 open,
0.35 slope, 0.33 shelf), because the upper bins carry most of it. Coastal
water is sampled mostly by fixed moorings, so few whole coastal profiles
exist to train or test on.
:::
